content_blocks.text: Do we have to use the Cabinet Office SQ?
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
Do we have to use the Cabinet Office SQ?

content_blocks.text: Yes.
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
Do we have to use the Cabinet Office SQ?

content_blocks.text: It is possible to deviate from the core questions included in it, but this will need to be reported as a "reportable deviation", in accordance with the guidance.
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015

content_blocks.text: Separate SQ stage for under-threshold contract - No longer possible?
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
Separate SQ stage for under-threshold contract - No longer possible?

content_blocks.text: Yes, Regulation 111 states that it is no longer possible to hold a separate selection stage for an under-threshold contract.
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
Separate SQ stage for under-threshold contract - No longer possible?

content_blocks.text: Is there a requirement to publish our SQ anywhere?
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
Is there a requirement to publish our SQ anywhere?

content_blocks.text: Yes - the SQ forms part of the "procurement documents" and as such will need to be available electronically from the date of the FTS advertisement.
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
Is there a requirement to publish our SQ anywhere?

content_blocks.text: Shall we disclose our SQ scoring system in the tender documentation?
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
Shall we disclose our SQ scoring system in the tender documentation?

content_blocks.text: Case law suggests that this is necessary in order to create transparency, and the Cabinet Office guidance states that "The contracting authority must ensure that full details including scoring for each question, weightings and any ‘pass mark’ or minimum threshold for selection are made known to the suppliers at the same time that the SQ/ selection questions are issued.
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
Shall we disclose our SQ scoring system in the tender documentation?

content_blocks.text: In addition, if certain questions are sufficiently critical that an unsatisfactory answer may lead to exclusion, irrespective of the score on the rest of the SQ, this should be made clear to suppliers."
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
Shall we disclose our SQ scoring system in the tender documentation?

content_blocks.text: What criteria can we use at SQ stage?
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
What criteria can we use at SQ stage?

content_blocks.text: The criteria that can be used are set out in the Cabinet Office SQ. This consists of various mandatory/discretionary exclusion criteria, followed by criteria around economic and financial standing and technical and professional ability.
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
What criteria can we use at SQ stage?

content_blocks.text: As part of the latter there is the possibility of including project specific questions aimed at eliciting technical and professional ability, provided that these are relevant and proportionate to the procurement and are framed around the topic areas listed at Regulation 60(9)(b) – (k) and must also meet the “relevant and proportionate” test.
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
What criteria can we use at SQ stage?

content_blocks.text: Finally, the Cabinet Office SQ also contains "additional modules" at sections 7(B-E), covering issues such as health and safety and environmental management - note that these must also pass the “relevant and proportionate” test before they can be included.
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
What criteria can we use at SQ stage?

content_blocks.text: We ask suppliers for recent accounts but do not read them. Is this okay?
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
We ask suppliers for recent accounts but do not read them. Is this okay?

content_blocks.text: No. Information should only be requested at SQ stage if it will actually be used as part of the selection process.
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015

content_blocks.text: Can we reject a bidder that plans to form a consortium or to sub-contract?
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
Can we reject a bidder that plans to form a consortium or to sub-contract?

content_blocks.text: No, but the standard SQ does allow you to ask questions about the proposed consortium/subcontractor and the proposed supply chain.
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015

content_blocks.text: How much discretion do we have to deselect bidders at SQ stage?
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
How much discretion do we have to deselect bidders at SQ stage?

content_blocks.text: Contracting authorities should only deselect bidders if they do not comply with the published selection criteria; de-selection must not be arbitrary. Where stated in the FTS notice, the contracting authority can limit the number of bidders invited to participate in the ITT stage, subject to the minimum number requirements set out at Regulation 65 (see next question for more detail) and to setting out in the procurement documentation the objective and non-discriminatory criteria that will be used to make this limitation in numbers.
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
How much discretion do we have to deselect bidders at SQ stage?

content_blocks.text: How many bidders do we need to send the ITT to?
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
FAQs
How many bidders do we need to send the ITT to?

content_blocks.text: In the restricted procedure, at least five (assuming five or more suitable suppliers respond). You should ensure that the FTS notice states any maximum number to which you are proposing to send the ITT, and the objective and non-discriminatory criteria to be used to limit the number selected. In the competitive with negotiation, competitive dialogue and innovation partnership procedures, the invitation to negotiate/participate in dialogue should be sent to at least three bidders.
heading_path: Selection stage under the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
